editorial.headline: Private Training for Agriculture and Fisheries: Bali’s PMA Position
editorial.standfirst: Private vocational training across agriculture and fisheries is nationally open to full foreign ownership; in Bali, the Large-scale OSS risk places it outside the provincial PMA moratorium.
editorial.body:
Private agricultural and fisheries job training is a broad vocational activity built around practical capability. Its scope covers skills and expertise in agricultural mechanisation, food crops, horticulture, mixed farming, land processing and conservation, crop cultivation, fishing, fish farming, fisheries machinery, and the processing of agricultural, fisheries and livestock outputs. It also includes production agribusiness for crops, livestock and aquatic resources. The defining feature is the training itself: a private organiser delivers programmes intended to add working skills across these fields. The activity follows the practical arc of agriculture and fisheries, from land and cultivation through catching, aquaculture, machinery, processing and production-focused agribusiness.

The record opens this activity to private organisers at every declared scale: Micro, Small, Medium and Large. That breadth does not dilute the underlying boundary. The activity remains vocational training aimed at building expertise in the listed agricultural and fisheries disciplines, delivered by a private provider. Scale determines the range at which the activity may be registered; the stated scope determines what the activity is. For founders, that is the useful reading: the record accommodates a full span of operating sizes while remaining anchored to practical, sector-specific skill development.

Nationally, the PMA position is direct. The status is TERBUKA, with maximum foreign ownership of 100%. In plain terms, foreign ownership may reach the full 100% national ceiling for this activity. Bali does not reverse that result. The province permanently blocks PMA registrations for Low and Medium-Low risk activities island-wide, but this activity is not marked as blocked. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK and, at the Large scale, its OSS risk is Medium-High/High; the record therefore states that it is not blocked by the moratorium.

The conclusion is appropriately narrow and clear. This is private vocational training for practical agricultural and fisheries capability, available across the full set of declared scales and nationally open to PMA up to 100% foreign ownership. In Bali, the record does not place it behind the province-wide PMA moratorium block. The Large-scale risk position is the stated reason, and no further Bali-side condition is supplied in the record.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally open to 100% foreign ownership, this private training activity is not blocked by Bali’s PMA moratorium.
